reuse.why: The preview reuses getApproxNumberThreshold, but all four changed amount consumers bypass the existing getScheduledAmount abstraction instead of evolving it.

duplication.why: Amount normalization is independently implemented in the API model, budget template, forecast normalization, and preview generation.

placement.why: The shared schedule amount policy is scattered across serialization and consumer modules despite shared/schedules.ts already housing getScheduledAmount.

scope.why: The edits remain focused on expected schedule amounts, their API representation, and associated tests.

maintainability.why: Successive policy changes update only one of several independent implementations, leaving maintainers multiple competing definitions to discover and synchronize.

bypasses_abstraction.where: scheduleModel.toExternal, createScheduleList, normalizeSchedule, and computeSchedulePreviewTransactions implement amount resolution locally rather than extending and calling shared/schedules.ts:getScheduledAmount.

disguised_duplication.where: The same amount-resolution decision appears under _amount, amountValue, and amountCondition.value, with type-based versus operator-based dispatch and differently shaped endpoint comparisons.

abstraction_drift.where: The four changed consumers retain independent amount policies while getScheduledAmount remains unchanged; later approximate and lowest-value rules are embedded only in computeSchedulePreviewTransactions.
